transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Huxley Head of ML), Carlos Mendez (Huxley Infra), Priya Rao (Huxley CTO)
Recorded at: 2026-03-24T15:00:00Z

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs customer's baseline provider (referred to as 'baseline' / 'current provider'), discuss tuning steps (batching, quantization, cache), and align on next steps for pilot progression. Action items captured at end.

Topics:
- Benchmarks: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps / tokens/sec)
- Differences vs baseline provider
- Tuning: batching, KV/prefix cache, quant profiles
- Cost implications and pricing for pilot
- Security/questions for Private/Dedicated options

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick roll call - Alex here, Samir with me from the SE side.
[00:07] Dana: Dana here.
[00:09] Carlos: Carlos.
[00:10] Priya: Priya on.
[00:12] Alex: Great. Samir, do you want to kick off with a quick summary of the numbers from last week's runs?
[00:18] Samir: Yeah sure - I pushed the updated runs into the shared sheet, link in the invite, but quick highlights: comparing our Redwood-hosted profile against their baseline provider for the 1.3B conversational model they wanted - on 1k concurrent users equivalent load.
[00:31] Samir: P50 latency we saw around 110ms on Redwood, baseline was 130ms. P95 Redwood 240ms vs baseline 310ms. P99 Redwood 420ms vs baseline 490ms. Throughput wise, on steady-state we saw about 1800 tokens/sec aggregate on our config, baseline was roughly 1500 tokens/sec.
[00:48] Dana: Okay that's promising. Can you remind us about the sequence lengths and prompt composition you used? Ours is usually 64 tokens prompt, 128 tokens generation avg - so about 192 total tokens.
[00:58] Samir: Yep we used that distribution - mix of short and medium, about 60% short, 40% medium. The runs include cold-starts and warmed runs. Cold starts bumped p99 a bit, as you would expect.
[01:12] Carlos: Was caching enabled for the Redwood runs? Our baseline has a prefix cache for common system prompts.
[01:18] Samir: We ran two modes: cache-off and cache-on. The numbers I quoted are cache-on with prefix/KV caching enabled. With cache-off p95 jumped to about 320ms, p99 to 600ms. So cache helps a lot for repeated system prompts, which seems consistent with what you saw.
[01:31] Priya: And what about batching? You mentioned continuous batching earlier. How aggressive was it? Latency SLO is critical for us so we can't batch too long.
[01:40] Samir: We tuned the batching window to 12ms max and adaptive batching so small bursts don't wait long. That gave us the throughput gains without pushing median latency much. We can tighten to 6ms but that lowers throughput ~12%. There's always the cost vs latency tradeoff.
[01:54] Alex: To add, Redwood's smart routing also helps - on these runs everything was on a single region, single model variant. If you wanted cheaper fallbacks we can show multi-variant routing that reduces cost but increases median latency a small amount.
[02:07] Dana: Very helpful. Do we have p95/p99 for the baseline under cache-on as well? Want an apples-to-apples.
[02:13] Samir: Yes baseline with similar cache settings: p95 320ms, p99 550ms. So relative improvements are roughly 10-25% on p95 and 5-10% on p99 depending on workload.
[02:24] Dana: Nice. Any variability across time of day - peak vs off-peak?
[02:28] Samir: We ran a 2-hour ramp test; variability low on Redwood hosted since the runner for the pilot is isolated for the test. Baseline provider showed slightly higher variance during synthetic peak spikes in their reported runs.
[02:41] Carlos: One thing we care about: vertical scaling vs horizontal. If we hit higher concurrency, does Redwood favor larger instances or more replicas? Network and memory on our infra are tight.
[02:52] Samir: For this model and traffic profile, we recommend horizontal replicas with autoscale up to N workers. That keeps memory footprint stable. If you want fewer replicas, we can use a larger GPU instance but cost goes up. We can show both cost scenarios in the sheet.
[03:06] Priya: On cost: what's the estimated per-1M-token cost in your pilot numbers vs baseline?
[03:12] Alex: In the pilot pricing we modeled, Redwood-hosted with current config is about $14 per 1M tokens. Baseline provider their published run is $18 per 1M tokens given similar batching; with fallback and lower quant it could be $12 but with quality tradeoffs. We'll send the updated pricing sheet.
[03:29] Dana: Are those numbers including KV cache savings?
[03:32] Alex: Yes the cost model factors in cache hit rates. For your workload we used an estimated 28% cache hit rate based on the sample traces you provided.
[03:41] Dana: We can validate that with more traces - I'll try to pull a week's worth with PII redacted.
[03:47] Carlos: Security quick note: we want to confirm encryption at rest keys - are you using customer-managed KMS in the pilot?
[03:54] Samir: For the hosted pilot we used Redwood-managed keys but can enable CMK for Private/Dedicated pilots. For enterprise-grade you can use KMS/HSM and we can provide audit logs.
[04:06] Priya: Good. Also SOC2 scope - we asked the security pack last week, any open items?
[04:11] Alex: I sent the core pack and the questionnaire answers. Dana, I think you had a question about data retention settings?
[04:17] Dana: Yeah just want to ensure transcripts/logs retention is configurable to 30 days for the pilot.
[04:21] Samir: Configurable - yes, retention policy can be set per-tenant and we can set it to 30 days for the pilot and change after contract.
[04:29] Alex: Back to benchmarks - Samir, can you walk the group through the attached chart - the p99 waterfall?
[04:35] Samir: Sure - slide 1 in the sheet shows stacked latencies: network, model compute, tokenization, and batching wait. On Redwood compute is smaller by ~18ms on average due to kernel selections and our quant path. Batching wait contributes ~8-12ms depending on window. Baseline provider shows larger compute time on p99 spikes.
[04:53] Dana: Is that likely due to model kernel optimization differences?
[04:57] Samir: Exactly - small differences in attention kernel and memory layout can change tail latency. Also we use an optimized KV cache implementation which reduces recompute on repeats.
[05:07] Carlos: About quantization - we've been conservative on quality. How did int8 affect accuracy in your eval?
[05:14] Samir: We ran a quality eval: int8 had a ~0.6% drop on BLEU-like metric for your reranking tasks, and subjective scoring showed minor differences on a few edge cases. For most flows int8 looked acceptable, but we recommended per-case validation. The sheet includes delta columns.
[05:29] Priya: If int8 is acceptable, what are the latency/cost improvements?
[05:33] Samir: Int8 reduces latency ~12% and cost ~20% in our test harness. For p95 it drops from 240ms to ~210ms on Redwood.
[05:42] Dana: That's compelling. For the pilot we want to keep quality very tight. Can we do a small holdout set of 500 queries and compare outputs side-by-side?
[05:50] Samir: Absolutely - if you provide the 500 redacted queries we can run int8 vs fp16 and produce a diff report.
[05:56] Dana: I'll get that to you by Friday.
[05:59] Alex: Great. A couple of housekeeping items: we'll update the benchmark sheet, Samir will run a 2x synthetic load test for worst-case p99 numbers and share by next Tuesday. Dana will send the holdout queries and the traffic distribution. Alex will send pricing and pilot contract.
[06:12] Carlos: One more question - have you tested Dedicated vs Hosted differences? If we go Dedicated on our VPC, are latencies better?
[06:19] Samir: Dedicated gives you isolation and potentially lower variance since you control the pool. Latency medians similar but tail is often tighter. Network egress from VPC may add slight overhead depending on topology. For regulated data, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[06:33] Priya: Good to know. We'll evaluate after pilot.
[06:36] Alex: Any other questions?
[06:38] Dana: No, just to confirm the timeline: holdout set by Friday, Samir's 2x run by next Tue, follow-up sync week of 3/30.
[06:46] Alex: Yep. Thanks everyone. We'll capture action items in the sheet.
[06:51] (end)
